examples.before:
# troupe settings
model: opus  # default model
retry: 3
agents:
  coder:
    temperature: 0.2
examples.input: `config watch` (with TROUPE_ACTOR=human:owner), then three hand edits to .troupe/troupe.yml: `model: opus` -> `sonnet`, then `retry: [3` (broken YAML), then `retry: 5`; then Ctrl-C (SIGINT)

results.1: All four arms print one line on stdout, `watching /theatre` (the full directory path), and nothing else. The two good edits print nothing.
results.2: Both arms print one line on stdout, `watching .` (relative path, not the full directory), and nothing else. The two good edits print nothing.

examples.input: the broken edit `retry: [3` while watch is running

results.1: Nothing on stdout. All four arms report it on stderr, each worded differently. One arm: `/theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml: invalid YAML: while parsing a flow sequence, expected ',' or ']', but got ':' (line 4, column 7)`. One arm: `troupe: .troupe/troupe.yml: invalid YAML (line 4, column 7): expected ',' or ']', but got ':'`. One arm: `troupe: cannot parse /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml: expected ',' or ']', but got ':' at line 4`. One arm prints the parser's full multi-line dump, starting `troupe: error: /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml: invalid YAML: while parsing a flow sequence` and pointing at `retry: [3` and `agents:` with carets.
results.2: Nothing on stdout. Both arms report it on stderr. One arm prints a single line with no location and no reason: `troupe: /theatre/.troupe/troupe.yml: invalid YAML: while parsing a flow sequence`. The other prints the full multi-line parser dump, starting `troupe: ./.troupe/troupe.yml: invalid YAML: while parsing a flow sequence`.

results.1: It stops in every arm. Three arms exit 0; one arm exits 137.
results.2: It stops in both arms. One arm exits 0; one arm exits 137.

results.1: exit 0 in all arms. Three import entries, then `model` opus->sonnet and `retry` 3->5, both `via: file`. The broken edit left no entry. Actor is recorded as `unknown`, even though watch ran with TROUPE_ACTOR=human:owner.
results.2: Same in both arms: three import entries, then `model` opus->sonnet and `retry` 3->5 via file, no entry for the broken edit, actor `unknown`.

context.in_practice: On both routes, watch prints only its start line, so the only way to see what it recorded is `config history`. The routes differ mainly in that line: route 1 names the full directory, while route 2 prints `.`. On both routes the error for a broken edit appears only on stderr and its wording differs from arm to arm; one route-2 arm gives no line number or reason. On each route, one arm exits 137 instead of 0 on Ctrl-C.
context.stakes: `config watch` runs in the background and records hand edits to the config file. The question is what it prints while it runs: anything a script reads from its output depends on that line, and a user has to be able to tell when a broken edit was not recorded.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: the start line names the full directory, but you have to run history to see what was recorded. Route 2: the same quiet output with a less informative `watching .` line, and in one arm a broken-edit error with no location.

plan_why: Records everything watch prints to stdout and stderr during one session: start, a hand edit that changes a value, an edit that breaks the YAML, an edit that fixes it (changing another value), then SIGINT. Afterwards, history shows which edits were recorded as events, and a file listing shows what state watch left under .troupe. Route 1 should print only the `watching` line on stdout, put the broken-YAML diagnostic on stderr, keep running, and exit 0.
routes: Only the watching line; diagnostics on stderr; events visible through history
